title: GroundCascade: Selective Second Opinions for GUI Grounding
why: Training-free controller consults a second GUI grounder only when full-screen and zoomed predictions disagree, on ScreenSpot-Pro and OSWorld-G.
mechanism: GUI grounding: agreement between a grounder's full-screen and zoomed predictions gates whether to query a complementary model; an optional Finalizer uses an unmarked joint crop when disagreement remains (Full vs Selective).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: 85.33% on ScreenSpot-Pro with Indeed-UI-32B/8B/32B and 88.43% on visible-target OSWorld-G-Refined with Qwen3.6-27B/3.8-27B/3.8-27B (+2.66 / +2.35 over the stronger standalone two-pass grounder); 72.20% category-balanced on UI-Vision (Selective 72.28%); Full mode 2.42-2.73 calls/request, 31-39% fewer than always using both models' two-pass predictions.

title: Deep Personalization: Continuous Context Observation for Local Proactive Agents
why: A proactive desktop agent observes on-device activity and learns when to intervene, evaluated on OSWorld-Persona from computer-use traces.
mechanism: Coco, a proactive desktop agent, uses a separate on-device Observer that monitors desktop activity, keeps compact long-term user context, and adapts intervention timing from implicit signals (engagement, dismissal, requests, repeated work) without streaming raw activity off-device.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: OSWorld-Persona is synthesized from computer-use trajectories with persona-conditioned intervention labels; deep personalization raises macro F1 from 0.12-0.19 (direct prompting) to 0.35-0.48 after adaptation (2.4-3.0x) across three backbones; week-long user study macro-averaged F1 0.199→0.515.

title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
why: Survey of self-evolving multimodal agents treats GUI and web navigation as a core scenario, comparing how experience, feedback, and updates transfer.
mechanism: Positions self-evolving multimodal agents (experience generation, feedback acquisition, update consolidation) across four scenarios, one of which is GUI and Web navigation, and judges whether self-improvement mechanisms are portable, conditional, blocked, or redundant under cross-scenario transfer.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported as a survey/analysis (44 pages, 15 tables, 4 figures); no new agent leaderboard numbers in the abstract; transfer verdicts are qualitative and described as still untested pending matched-budget measurements.

title: IntentTwin: Deconfounding Candidate Support and the Oracle-to-Deployment Gap in Offline Web Behavior Prediction
why: Shows Mind2Web-style offline web-action reranking can be confounded by candidate support, and tests support-balanced sets plus DOM/LM proposers.
mechanism: Formalizes support-identifiability rate (SIR) in offline web-behavior candidate reranking, builds support-balanced candidate sets, and evaluates a target-free dual-path proposer that combines support retrieval with open-vocabulary DOM/LM proposals, including a Mind2Web audit.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported on filtered OPeRA (4,282/469/992 steps): original protocol SIR 1.0000 on target-OOV rows; support balancing reduces SIR to 0.0000; strongest conditional reranker 0.7214 Exact@1 overall (0.7988 IV / 0.5668 OOV); dual-path Proposal Recall@16 0.6915 and end-to-end Exact@1 0.5212 vs oracle 0.7450. On Mind2Web, SIR 0.2380 and oracle-to-proposal gap 0.2125.

title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
why: Gates web-agent memory updates as falsifiable hypotheses before they are committed, with results on WebArena plus app and tool-use tasks.
mechanism: FGSE treats each experience-derived memory update as a structured hypothesis (precondition, behavior change, expected effect, verifier), applies it only in a temporary state, tests transfer/falsification/regression probes, then commits, refines, or rejects it — changing when a web agent may persist lessons.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: 39.8 WebArena success, 78.8 AppWorld average completion, and 0.724/0.487 Pass^1 on τ-Retail/τ-Airline; falsification failures 5.0%, regression damage 1.3%, harmful committed updates 3.6%.
